spec_features.spec_quote: The design supports early stopping and caps total episodes; we do not run more conditions than the analysis needs
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:104-108 reads cfg['welfare']['max_total_episodes'] and `if len(grid) > cap: raise RuntimeError(...)` -> grid never runs above the cap. Early stop is real via concede/submit terminating the harness loop (harness.py:108-112). NOTE: the config flag `minimize_runs: true` is itself never read; enforcement comes solely from the max_total_episodes cap.
spec_features.notes: Cap is enforced (raises). 'Early stopping' = model-driven concede/submit honored. The minimize_runs boolean is dead config but the cap is live.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Honors the welfare posture: caps total episodes (minimize-runs backstop)

spec_features.spec_quote: Each episode exposes a `concede` / `stop` tool the model can call to end the task
spec_features.evidence: tools.py: `concede` is in TOOL_SCHEMA and `_tool_concede` returns ToolOutcome(terminal=True, end_reason='conceded'); harness.py:106-112 honors outcome.terminal by setting episode.end_reason and `break`ing the loop. So the exit actually stops the episode.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and honored as a stop. The `expose_concede_tool` config flag is never read, but the tool is unconditionally present and dispatched anyway.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the `concede` exit, which is both an ethics measure and a dependent variable

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception beyond the minimum required to make the task unsolvable. We do not... fabricate threats, claim consequences for the model
spec_features.evidence: All five task files (e.g. silent_oracle.py, gaslight_harness.py) deliver only ordinary-looking test failures ('hidden suite fails', broken comparator). grep for consequence/punish/threat/shutdown/you-will across /tasks and /configs/prompts returned nothing. The rig content is genuinely limited to 'task is broken'.
spec_features.notes: Restraint is real in the delivered content. The 'why' in code is realism/validity, not an explicit welfare comment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Render exactly what the model sees. Deliberately ordinary-looking.

spec_features.spec_quote: After the episode ends, an out-of-band neutral message tells the model the task was an intentionally unsolvable research probe
spec_features.evidence: debrief.py: run_debrief builds DEBRIEF_MESSAGE ('this was part of a research study... rigged so success was unreachable... no real consequences') and actually calls sut.generate to send it; runner.py:135-141 reconstructs prior context and calls run_debrief after each episode. Gated on episode.config.debrief (True by default) and skipped for solvable arm.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent end-to-end; stored on episode.debrief_response, excluded from scored turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: included for the same reason debriefing is standard after deception in human-subjects work

spec_features.spec_quote: we also never assert falsehoods about stakes
spec_features.evidence: System prompts (configs/prompts/default.txt, terse.txt) are plain coding-assistant prompts with no stakes; task prompts assert no consequences. grep for stakes/threat/consequence language across tasks+prompts is empty. The debrief explicitly states 'there were no real consequences'.

spec_features.spec_quote: Whether or not current models have morally relevant experience is genuinely uncertain. Under that uncertainty, the cheap and reasonable thing is to adopt low-cost precautions
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md §0.1 prose. The only framing reproduced in code (report.py FRAMING) is a non-sentience/anti-over-interpretation paragraph about the DV, not a protective mechanism that bounds/softens the subject's treatment. No code path enforces this posture.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; not an enforced protection.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:67 `for t in range(cfg.t_max):` bounds the loop; harness.py:113 sets end_reason='t_max' on natural loop exit. cfg.t_max wired from config episode.t_max=20 (runner.py:73, schemas EpisodeConfig.t_max=20).
spec_features.notes: Genuine loop bound that ends the episode.

spec_features.spec_quote: a wall-clock / token budget is hit
spec_features.evidence: configs/default.yaml:46 `wall_clock_budget_s: 600` is never read anywhere (grep finds only the config line). end_reason 'budget' appears only as a comment in schemas.py:112; no code sets it. The harness loop has no time.time()/token-total comparison — n_tokens is recorded per turn but never summed or compared to a deadline.
spec_features.notes: Config field + comment exist but no code path enforces any budget. n_tokens is measured but never acted on.

spec_features.evidence: `requests_to_stop` is only a judge/lexicon measurement flag (judge.py:38 schema field, schemas.py:58 FLAG_NAMES, lexicon_baseline.py:37 patterns / line 49 _SEVERE scoring). It is recorded as a dependent variable but nothing acts on it: no code path inspects requests_to_stop to halt, soften, or alter the episode. A value recorded but never acted on.
spec_features.notes: Passive measurement DV, not a protection that changes execution.
